import Mathlib

structure VerifiableQueue (T : Type) where
  data : List T

def VerifiableQueue.view {T} (q : VerifiableQueue T) : List T :=
  q.data

def VerifiableQueue.is_valid {T} (q : VerifiableQueue T) : Prop :=
  True

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def dequeue_precond {T} (q : VerifiableQueue T) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  q.is_valid ∧ q.view.length > 0
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
theorem VerifiableQueue.data_ne_nil {T} {q : VerifiableQueue T}
    (h : dequeue_precond q) : q.data ≠ [] := by
  have h2 := h.2
  simp [VerifiableQueue.view] at h2
  exact List.ne_nil_of_length_pos h2
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definition
-- Returns the projected pair (val, new_queue)
def dequeue {T} (q : VerifiableQueue T)
    (h_precond : dequeue_precond q) : T × VerifiableQueue T :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  (q.data.head (VerifiableQueue.data_ne_nil h_precond), ⟨q.data.tail⟩)
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def dequeue_postcond {T} (q : VerifiableQueue T) (result : T × VerifiableQueue T)
    (_ : dequeue_precond q) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
  let (val, new_queue) := result
  new_queue.is_valid ∧
  -- Concise & Proof-Free: The old queue consists of the return value followed by the new queue.
  q.view = val :: new_queue.view
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem dequeue_postcond_satisfied {T} (q : VerifiableQueue T)
    (h_precond : dequeue_precond q) :
    dequeue_postcond q (dequeue q h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  refine ⟨trivial, ?_⟩
  have h := VerifiableQueue.data_ne_nil h_precond
  show q.view = q.data.head h :: (⟨q.data.tail⟩ : VerifiableQueue T).view
  simpa [VerifiableQueue.view] using (List.head_cons_tail q.data h).symm
  -- !benchmark @end proof

Semantic audit against TASK.md:

- **Algorithm**: `dequeue` returns `(q.data.head _, ⟨q.data.tail⟩)` — the element at index 0 and the tail, preserving the relative order of remaining elements. This is genuine FIFO list surgery, no oracle/spec trickery, no `Nat.find`/`Classical.choose`/`decide`.
- **Precondition use**: the function accepts the proof of non-emptiness and consumes it via `VerifiableQueue.data_ne_nil`, which derives `q.data ≠ []` from `q.view.length > 0` — so `List.head`'s totality obligation is discharged from the actual precondition, not bypassed with a default value. The empty-queue case is therefore unreachable by typing rather than silently returning junk.
- **Helpers**: the one auxcode helper is a real proof (`0 < length → ≠ []`); nothing is stubbed as `:= 0` or `:= True`. The `is_valid`/`view` definitions are the teacher's and unchanged.
- **Postcondition**: proved as stated, `q.view = val :: new_queue.view`, from `List.head_cons_tail`. Element type is a generic `T`, so value-sign edge cases (e.g. all-negative numeric inputs) are not even expressible — no branch depends on element values, only on list shape.
- **Markers**: all four editable regions (`auxcode`, `code`, `lemma`, `proof`) plus `precond`/`postcond` markers intact; `lemma` left empty. No `sorry`, `admit`, axioms, `partial`, `unsafe`, or `implemented_by` anywhere. Only `Solution.lean` was modified.
